text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] PagerDuty P1 triggered — control-plane heartbeat missing for availability-zone az4 (us-west-2). Auto-retries: 3. Affected service: routing-control-plane. Link: https://pd.redwood.example/INC-2311112222 :rotating_light:

pagerduty: Incident INC-2311112222 created and assigned to oncall-ryan. Priority: P1. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/control-plane-heartbeat.md

oncall-ryan: ack'd. I'm taking pager. Starting initial triage — pulling control-plane metrics and pod status.

emma_devops: I'm seeing control-plane API latency spike and a bunch of heartbeat timeouts from az4 nodes in telemetry. Confirmed increased 5xx rate for routing-control-plane.

sara_infra: network fabric shows partial loss of heartbeat packets between az3 and az4 around 23:45 UTC. BGP flaps in our fabric controller logs. Suspect intermittent overlay issue.

oncall-ryan: quick snapshot of pods in az4 control-plane pool:
```
$ kubectl -n control-plane get pods -o wide --field-selector=spec.nodeName=az4-node-
control-plane-0   CrashLoopBackOff   0/1   10d   10.2.1.4
control-plane-1   Running            1/1   10d   10.2.1.5
control-plane-2   Unknown            0/1   10d   10.2.1.6
```

emma_devops: logs from control-plane-0 show connection errors to fabric-proxy and repeated "heartbeat timed out" entries.

joel_support: customer-impact telemetry: hosted API error rate in us-west-2 +5.6% over baseline last 10m, median latency +120ms. 12 dedicated customers currently reporting degraded in-region behaviour (support tickets auto-tagged). No broad billing impact yet.

oncall-ryan: mitigation plan: 1) activate routing fallback to az2 for region us-west-2 (degrades latency but restores success rate), 2) spin up replacement control-plane nodes in az5 (cross-AZ), 3) start controlled drain of suspect az4 nodes, 4) notify customers via status page if impact persists >30m. Executing step 1 now.

pager-kim: Note — per escalation policy, will escalate to SRE lead in 10 minutes if not resolved.

emma_devops: issuing routing toggle (deconf mode) now: `redwood-routes set-fallback --region us-west-2 --from az4 --to az2 --force`

incident-bot: Action logged: routing fallback activated for us-west-2. All new requests from az4 are being routed to az2 and az5 per policy.

sara_infra: concurrently opening ticket with network fabric team to trace BGP fabric between az3/az4. Kicking off traceroutes.

oncall-ryan: starting replacement nodes in az5: `infractl scale control-plane --region us-west-2 --az az5 --count 3`

maria_sre: heads-up: enable degraded mode for session-caching layer to avoid cache write storms during reschedule. `configctl set service/session-cache --mode degraded`

emma_devops: degraded mode enabled. Cache TTL extended, write-back disabled.

joel_support: posted an initial customer note: "We are aware of increased errors and latencies in us-west-2 caused by an infrastructure network issue. Traffic is being rerouted to maintain service; some customers may see higher latency. We'll post updates every 15 minutes." Link: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/2311112222

pagerduty: Acknowledgement recorded. Incident still active. Escalation scheduled in 9 minutes.

oncall-ryan: quick health check after fallback: success rate in us-west-2 recovered to +1% above baseline, latency back to +40ms over baseline. Live graph: https://metrics.redwood.example/d/us-west-2/control-plane

sara_infra: fabric trace shows intermittent packet loss on spine switch S-az4-07 at 23:45 UTC; we're coordinating with colo ops to power-cycle the switch as a last resort after change window approval.

maria_sre: recommend holding failover to full-region active DR; current fallback keeps stateful KPIs within tolerances. Proceeding with node reschedules and monitoring for split-brain.

oncall-ryan: initiating drain of control-plane-0 and control-plane-2 in az4 and letting autoscaling create replacements in az5.

emma_devops: drain commands issued: `kubectl drain control-plane-0 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl drain control-plane-2 ...`

joel_support: updating ticket queue and sending targeted emails to the 12 affected dedicated customers with mitigation steps and ETA 30–45m.

pager-kim: escalation triggered to SRE lead (maria_sre) — acknowledged.

maria_sre: I'm on the call. prioritizing fabric replacement and node reprovisioning. If the spine doesn't recover within 20m, we'll request emergency colo access to replace S-az4-07.

oncall-ryan: current estimated customer impact window 20–40 minutes assuming fallback and replacements hold. Will post a timeline once autoscaling stabilizes.

incident-bot: Next automated update scheduled in 15m.

maria_sre: post-mitigation note: observed steady state at 23:58 UTC after fallback and node reprovisioning — error rate normalized to baseline, sustained success rate restored. We'll keep the fallback routing active for an hour and then ramp traffic back gradually. Filing follow-up action items: network postmortem, improve fabric alerting, add a canary to detect az-level heartbeats earlier.

oncall-ryan: handing off to night-oncall (oncall-nina) at 00:30 UTC. Leaving runbook steps and checklist in the incident doc.

joel_support: closing customer-facing update with resolution note and link to postmortem ticket: https://pm.redwood.example/PM-2311112222

incident-bot: Incident INC-2311112222 resolved (auto-close pending 30m) — root cause suspected fabric spine hardware failure.

maria_sre: final note: follow-up postmortem scheduled tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Action owners assigned. Thanks all for quick response. :raised_hands:
